name: Rye Ocean Beach

facts.claim: Rye Ocean Beach lies in the heart of Mornington Peninsula National Park's coastline.
Powerful waves and numerous reef breaks make it popular with experienced surfers.
Visitors can walk the exposed sandy shoreline, look out across Bass Strait and spot shorebirds.

name: Coppins Track

facts.claim: Coppins Track is near Sorrento and overlooks Sorrento Ocean Beach, with stairs to a lookout platform.
It winds through coastal scrub along the coast to Diamond Bay.
A round trip starts and finishes at Sorrento Ocean Beach, which has toilets, barbecues, a cafe and a patrolled surf beach.

name: Mushroom Reef Marine Sanctuary

facts.claim: The 80 ha sanctuary at Flinders takes its name from its mushroom-shaped reef and extends about 1 km offshore.
Rockpools at Flinders are good for exploring Victoria's marine life, and snorkelling and diving on the subtidal reefs is popular.
All fishing and taking of animals, plants and artefacts is prohibited.

name: Alba Thermal Springs & Spa

facts.claim: Alba is a hot-springs and spa wellness destination on the Mornington Peninsula, set in native bushland.
It has outdoor geothermal pools including a rain pool and forest pools.
Private rooftop geothermal pools and spa treatments are also offered.

name: Penguin Parade

facts.claim: Phillip Island is home to the largest little penguin colony in the world.
Penguins waddle home from the sea to their burrows at sunset every night of the year, watched from viewing platforms and boardwalks.
Tickets should be booked in advance; ticket holders should arrive about an hour before penguin arrival time.
It is run by Phillip Island Nature Parks at Summerlands Beach.

name: Koala Conservation Centre

facts.claim: Two tree-top boardwalks (800 m and 600 m loops, about 20 minutes each) give close views of koalas in their natural habitat.
Six hectares of bushland trails also have wallabies, echidnas and native birds.
Run by Phillip Island Nature Parks; the operator now calls it the Koala Conservation Reserve.
